data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous topicals & wound care_

**Class:** Topical sex steroids

## Mechanism of action
- Testosterone: stimulates collagen and epidermal growth in genital skin
- Oestrogen: increases epidermal thickness, collagen and hydration in oestrogen-deficient skin and mucosa

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Testosterone 2% ointment: lichen sclerosus (historical — inferior to clobetasol; no longer recommended)
- Oestrogen: atrophic vaginitis/vulvovaginal atrophy, labial adhesions in girls; photoaged skin in post-menopausal women (cosmeceutical, limited)

## Dose & formulations
- Vaginal oestrogen cream as per gynaecological regimen

## Adverse effects
- Testosterone: virilisation (clitoral enlargement, hirsutism); oestrogen: breast tenderness, bleeding, systemic absorption

## Contraindications
- Hormone-dependent cancers, pregnancy

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated.

## Viva points
- Topical testosterone for lichen sclerosus is obsolete — clobetasol is first-line

_Sources: Khopkar ch.28 (Topical testosterone, oestrogen); Wolverton 4e ch.45. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
